text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000533 bills 99215 far above risk-adjusted expectation, often on low-complexity patients, but the few documented charts support the billed levels, so the pattern is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern raises concern. The 99215 share is elevated in every complexity band, including patients with zero conditions. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims carry routine diagnoses such as low back pain (M54.50), UTI (N39.0) and URI (J06.9), for example C0285973, C0286006 and C0286082. Against that, the records review found no documented 99215 below the billed level. Charts for some of those same low-complexity claims (C0285995, C0286058, C0286064) show high MDM and 40+ minutes, and the moderate-plus data-reviewed notes all have lab or test lines on the claim, so there is no cloning signal. However, only 5 documented 99215 claims is too thin to clear the provider, and high-MDM notes on single-diagnosis back pain or UTI visits deserve scrutiny for inflated or templated documentation. A reviewer should first request charts for more of the 99215 claims, prioritizing repeat visits by the same patient (e.g., M0120490, billed 99215 three times for M54.50/N39.0). The reviewer should read whether the MDM narrative and time are clinically plausible for those presenting problems."}
